title_en: Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street Walk Onto a Stage…
title_zh: Vanguard、BlackRock、State Street 三巨头罕见同台：ETF 的下一个十年
subtitle_zh: Trillions 特别节目：Bloomberg ETFs in Depth 大会现场，掌管 35 万亿美元的三大 ETF 女性掌门人首次同台。
summary_zh: 本期 Trillions 现场录制于 Bloomberg ETFs in Depth 纽约大会，Joel Weber 与 Eric Balchunas 首次把 Vanguard 的 Janelle Jackson、BlackRock iShares 的 Elise Terry 与 State Street SPDR 的 Anna Paglia 请到同一舞台。三家合计管理约 35 万亿美元，占美国 ETF 市场约 70%。围绕 SPYM 以 2 个基点成为 Trump 账户默认 ETF，VTI 与 IVV 也入选，Elise 明确 IVV 降至 2bp 并非针对 SPYM。对 BlackRock 本周申报的 ETIF（交易所交易间隔基金），Anna 直言「又爱又恨」，Elise 解释其把间隔基金的私募灵活性与 ETF 交易所体验结合；Janelle 担心 15% 私募上限稀释敞口。Z 世代环节 Anna 分享同一位网红几分钟内先推 SPY 再推 VOO 的荒诞案例，强调必须进入 LLM。Elise 与 Anna 担心未受教育投资者被误导，Eric 提议参考电影分级的「红绿灯」标签。
description: Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street Walk Onto a Stage…

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios, podcasts, radio, news. Welcome to Trillions. I'm Joel Weber. And I'm Eric Balchunas. So this is a special episode of Trillions. We're recording live at Bloomberg's ETFs in depth in New York City. And it's really special because for the first time, I think, that we know of any event, we have the big three, Vanguard, BlackRock, and State Street on a stage for this special episode of Trillions.
turns.zh: Bloomberg Audio Studios，播客、广播、新闻。欢迎收听 Trillions。我是 Joel Weber。我是 Eric Balchunas。这是 Trillions 的一期特别节目，我们正在 Bloomberg 于纽约市举办的 ETFs in Depth 大会现场录制。这一期真的很特别，因为据我们所知，这是首次有任何一场活动能把三大巨头——Vanguard、BlackRock 和 State Street——请到同一个舞台上，来做这期 Trillions 特别节目。

turns.en: I'm all over the ETF circuit for like 20 years now, and I've never seen the three of them on stage together.
turns.zh: 我在 ETF 圈子里跑了差不多 20 年，从来没见过这三家同台亮相。

turns.en: So I believe it's a first.
turns.zh: 所以我相信这是头一回。

turns.en: If you're that veteran ETF and you've seen it, let me know.
turns.zh: 如果你是那位见过场面的资深 ETF 老兵，请告诉我们。

turns.en: But I do believe this is a first ever.
turns.zh: 但我确实相信这是史无前例的一次。

turns.en: Let me give you the numbers on these three firms, Joel.
turns.zh: Joel，让我给大家报一下这三家公司的数字。

turns.en: Ready? Bring it.
turns.zh: 准备好了吗？说来听听。

turns.en: $ 35 trillion.
turns.zh: 35 万亿美元。

turns.en: Right there. Okay? So don't make them mad. They also have.
turns.zh: 就这个数。好了？所以别惹她们生气。她们还掌握着——

turns.en: 70% market share of the U.S. ETF market, which we're going to discuss. And this is going to be very exciting. They're competitors, but also trying to.
turns.zh: 美国 ETF 市场 70% 的份额，这正是我们今天要讨论的话题。这场对话会非常精彩。她们既是竞争对手，同时也在努力把这块蛋糕——

turns.en: Grow the pie. Okay. They are Janelle Jackson of Vanguard, Elise Terry on the end from BlackRock, and Anna Paglia of State Street. So welcome to Trillions. You seem friendly backstage, but there was a metal detector and some stuff was confiscated. Nunchucks, brass knuckles, and a taser. Janelle, which one of those was yours?
turns.zh: 做大。好的。今天到场的三位嘉宾是：Vanguard 的 Janelle Jackson、坐在最边上的 BlackRock 的 Elise Terry，以及 State Street 的 Anna Paglia。欢迎做客 Trillions。你们在后台看起来很友好，但现场有金属探测器，有些东西被没收了——双节棍、指虎，还有一把电击枪。Janelle，哪一样是你的？

turns.en: I'm team nunchucks.
turns.zh: 我是双节棍队的。

turns.en: Nunchucks?
turns.zh: 双节棍？

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: I kind of thought so. So earlier, Eric talked about market share. The big three 10 years ago accounted for 80% of ETF assets. 10 years later, 70%. Is that plateauing or slipping, Janelle?
turns.zh: 我就猜到是这样。刚才 Eric 提到了市场份额。十年前，三巨头占 ETF 资产的 80%；十年后的今天，是 70%。Janelle，这个数字是见顶了还是在下滑？

turns.en: I mean, I feel like this is a leading question, and you guys want me to say something that I'm not going to say. But I'm very happy to be here with these ladies and representing where investors want and choose to put their money. So I don't really measure success as far as it relates to cash flow or market share. But I think there's a lot of exciting things that are happening with ETF product, and I'm excited that we get to be a part of that.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是个诱导性问题，你们想让我说一些我并不会说的话。但我很高兴今天能和这两位女士一起坐在这里，代表投资者愿意选择、也确实选择把资金托付给我们的机构。所以我并不用现金流或市场份额来衡量成功。我认为 ETF 产品端正在发生很多令人兴奋的事情，我也很高兴我们能参与其中。

turns.en: Another thing Eric mentioned was this Gulliver Travels idea of like people coming for you. And I'm curious about that innovation. We see a lot of products. There's so many launches. There's a lot of closures. How do you keep your edge, Hannah?
turns.zh: Eric 刚才还提到一个「格列佛游记」式的说法，就是会有人来围攻你。我很好奇这一点——谈创新——市面上产品数量众多，新发行不少，清盘也不少。Anna，你怎么保持自己的优势？

turns.en: Well, it's easier than you think because what we do is really follow the trend and follow what our clients are telling.
turns.zh: 其实比你想象的要简单，因为我们要做的就是紧跟趋势、紧跟客户告诉——

turns.en: Us to do.
turns.zh: 我们要做的事情。

turns.en: In this industry right now, barriers to entry are really, really low, but barriers to success are really, really high. So if you do it well, you know it. You follow the money, you know it. Mass proliferation of products doesn't bother us, doesn't scare us because you know when you hit something that your clients really want.
turns.zh: 在当下的行业里，进入门槛真的非常低，但成功门槛真的非常高。所以只要你做得好，你就知道怎么做；只要跟着资金流走，你就知道怎么做。产品的大规模涌现不会困扰我们、也不会吓到我们，因为你能识别出哪些是客户真正想要的东西。

turns.en: Elise, how about for you at Asher's?
turns.zh: Elise，那 iShares 这边呢？

turns.en: Look, innovation is tremendous for this industry, right? It just means new ideas. It means more choice for our investors. It means just continuous innovation and new products coming out. However, I would say, right, there is a lot more sophisticated strategies that are coming out. And I think you really need to take a step deeper into how is this product constructed? How is this product going to trade? How is this product supposed to work in different markets, right? I think that the continued innovation is great. You asked the question to Janelle of market share. Look, the pie just keeps growing. That's awesome for everybody. It's awesome for investors. But I do think you have to take just a level deeper in the questions that you're asking. You know, I know some of the obvious stuff is like, what am I paying for the expense.
turns.zh: 你看，创新对这个行业来说意义非凡，对吧？它意味着新想法，意味着给投资者更多选择，意味着持续不断的创新和新产品问世。不过我想说，如今推出的策略要复杂得多。我觉得你真的需要更深入一层去看：这只产品是如何构建的？它会如何交易？在不同市场环境下它应该如何运作？我认为持续创新是好事。你刚才问 Janelle 关于市场份额的问题——你看，蛋糕只会越来越大，这对所有人都是好事，对投资者也是好事。但我确实认为，你在提问时要多下探一层。我知道那些最表面的问题，比如「这只 ETF 的费用率——

turns.en: Ratio for this ETF? but it goes far beyond that.
turns.zh: ——是多少？」但远远不止于此。

turns.en: Would you rather buy a three basis point product with a 25 basis point spread or do you want to buy a five basis point product with a two basis point spread? Like these are the things we need to continuously educate on as more and more products continue to come out.
turns.zh: 你是愿意买一只费率 3 个基点、但价差 25 个基点的产品，还是愿意买一只费率 5 个基点、价差只有 2 个基点的产品？随着越来越多新产品问世，这些都是我们需要持续做投资者教育的地方。

turns.en: Yeah, and I can.
turns.zh: 是的，我也——

turns.en: Also add something to that, which is I think that the word innovation is a little stale and it's a little overused because what.
turns.zh: 想补充一点：我觉得「创新」这个词已经有点陈旧、有点被滥用了，因为——

turns.en: We need to go for right now is really disruption.
turns.zh: 我们现在真正需要的其实是颠覆。

turns.en: Innovation, everything new, can be innovative, is it really disruptive?
turns.zh: 创新，任何新东西都能被称为创新，但它真的具有颠覆性吗？

turns.en: I don't think so. So let's look at disruption more so than innovation.
turns.zh: 我并不这么认为。所以让我们更多地去关注颠覆，而不是创新。

turns.en: And by the way, you want the big tree here, and you had three women?
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，你要凑齐三巨头，还请来了三位女性——

turns.en: You're brave.
turns.zh: 你胆子真大。

turns.en: You are really brave.
turns.zh: 你真的是胆子太大了。

turns.en: So the taser belonged to Anna.
turns.zh: 所以电击枪是 Anna 的。

turns.en: Wait, can I get a shot at this one too?
turns.zh: 等等，那这题我是不是也能答一下？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 好啊。

turns.en: No nunchucks. I mean, I think there's something to be said about the size of our organizations and what our product lineups look like. But at Vanguard, we're not going to be everything to everybody. And we're not always everyone's cup of tea. So it's great that investors have options to execute the ideas that they want. So I view us as like the friendly giants.
turns.zh: 不是双节棍那题。我是说，我觉得我们各家机构的规模和产品线本身也说明了一些问题。但在 Vanguard，我们不会试图为所有人做所有事，我们也并不总是所有人都喜欢的那杯茶。所以，投资者有各种选择去实现他们的想法，这是好事。我会把我们看作是「友善的巨人」。

turns.en: It's more like Atlas.
turns.zh: 更像是 Atlas（阿特拉斯）吧。

turns.en: We're a little bit of carrying the world on our shoulders. But when there are a lot of innovative products and you do think about things like spread and expense ratio and what it's really costing and what you really get, what we can really do and still be a part of as the giants is help with education and making sure that everyone's being responsible in the industry as we play our roles.
turns.zh: 我们有点像在把世界扛在肩上。但当市面上出现大量创新产品，当你去认真思考价差、费率、真正的成本和真正的收益时，作为「巨人」，我们真正能做、也仍然能做的一部分工作，就是投资者教育，以及确保行业里每个人都在扮演好自己的角色时保持尽责。

turns.en: Let me ask you about that, because when you talk to the big issuers and Schwab was on earlier and they're all like, well, we've got.
turns.zh: 我想追问一下这一点，因为当你和大型发行商交流时——Schwab 早些时候也在场——他们都会说，嗯，我们必须——

turns.en: To be careful.
turns.zh: 小心谨慎。

turns.en: And I think you said it, Janelle, ETF proliferation is a gift and a curse. Now, there's obviously some really wild products out there. Do you think because of 3x leverage prediction market ETF launches, that it changes anybody's view of VU, SPYM, or IVV? I personally don't think so. I don't think anybody in these funds cares. Simply like, okay, McDonald's exists, but you could eat, like people at Whole Foods aren't bothered that McDonald's exists down the street, or is there a danger of it contaminating the ETF brand?
turns.zh: Janelle，我记得你说过，ETF 产品的爆炸式增长既是恩赐也是诅咒。市面上显然有一些非常疯狂的产品。你觉得，鉴于现在有 3 倍杠杆的预测市场 ETF 之类的东西发行，这会改变任何人对 VOO、SPYM 或 IVV 的看法吗？我个人并不这么认为。我不觉得这些基金的持有人会在意。就好比说，OK，麦当劳存在，但你还是可以选择吃别的——就像 Whole Foods 的顾客不会因为街对面开了家麦当劳就感到困扰。或者说，这些产品会不会污染 ETF 这个品牌？

turns.en: Who wants to take a shot at that?
turns.zh: 谁想接一下这个问题？

turns.en: We'll start with you, Gerald, because I quoted you.
turns.zh: 我们从你开始，Janelle，因为我引用了你的话。

turns.en: You like to talk about products being hot sauce, and I always say we're like the cup of milk. Who eats a plate of hot sauce? But you can always load up on milk. I don't think it damages the wrapper. I know the ETF had a bit of a halo for a while because everything was indexed. And it's kind of like you look at the name, you look at the benchmark, you know what you own. And as markets have evolved and the industry's evolved, we've definitely gotten away from that. But that doesn't mean it's bad. It just means you have to go a little bit of an extra mile to know what you're buying. Make sure that you're educated.
turns.zh: 你（Eric）喜欢把产品比作辣椒酱，我一直说我们就像那杯牛奶。谁会吃一整盘辣椒酱呢？但你可以一直喝牛奶。我并不觉得这会损害 ETF 这个「包装」。我知道 ETF 曾经有一段时间自带光环，因为一切都是指数化的：你看名字、看基准，就知道自己持有什么。随着市场和行业的演进，我们确实已经离那种状态很远了。但这并不代表它变坏了，只是意味着你需要多花一点力气去了解自己到底在买什么，确保自己受到了足够的教育。

turns.en: I would agree with that. Education is paramount. I'm not a big fan of departing too much from the stated purpose of the ETF vehicle. Let's never forget where we came from. Why is the ETF wrapper so powerful? Diversification, low cost, tax efficiency. And then we started getting fancy. And, you know, the hot sauce started getting hotter and hotter and hotter.
turns.zh: 我同意这一点。投资者教育是至关重要的。我并不太赞成过度偏离 ETF 这个载体的初衷。让我们永远不要忘记自己是从哪里来的：ETF 这个包装为什么如此强大？分散化、低成本、税收效率。然后我们开始搞花活，辣椒酱变得越来越辣、越来越辣、越来越辣——

turns.en: And then you depart so.
turns.zh: ——直到你偏离——

turns.en: Much from your stated mission that at what point is too far. I think we are getting a little too far with those things.
turns.zh: 你的初衷太远，那么到什么程度就算太远了？我觉得我们在这些事情上已经有点走得太远了。

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: Friendly Giants. That's a good segue from London. We had a Trillions episode that we recorded in London earlier this year. For that one, we had Vanguard and BlackRock. We didn't have State Street. Now we have State Street. One of the things that's happened this year is that State Street has a certain ETF called SPYM, and that became the default ETF. for Trump accounts at two basis points, and undercut everyone. Janelle, how do you feel about that?
turns.zh: 「友善的巨人」——这是从伦敦那一期的一个很好的承接。今年早些时候我们在伦敦录过一期 Trillions，那一期请到了 Vanguard 和 BlackRock，没有 State Street。这次我们请到了 State Street。今年发生的一件事是，State Street 有一只叫 SPYM 的 ETF，它成为了 Trump 账户的默认 ETF，费率 2 个基点，把所有人都比下去了。Janelle，你怎么看？

turns.en: It was totally illogical for you to ask me the question.
turns.zh: 你问我这个问题完全不合逻辑啊。

turns.en: Did she have the taser? Did she have the taser? Nunchucks.
turns.zh: 她是不是拿着电击枪？她是不是拿着电击枪？双节棍呢？

turns.en: Are you gonna tase me?
turns.zh: 你要电我吗？

turns.en: We know Anne is happy about it. That's not interesting. We wanna see your reactions. And Elise, you're next.
turns.zh: 我们知道 Anna 对此很开心，这没什么意思。我们想看你们的反应。Elise，你下一个。

turns.en: Yeah, I would say, I mean, we were excited to be a part of the program.
turns.zh: 是的，我想说，我们很高兴能参与到这个项目里。

turns.en: I think it's a really unique opportunity for investors to start at the beginning of their lives, understanding what these products are and being involved in markets. I do a lot of talks about women and wealth and a lot of women's first investing opportunities are through their 401k and their employer.
turns.zh: 我认为这对投资者来说是一个非常独特的机会，让他们从人生一开始就理解这些产品是什么、参与到市场中来。我做过很多关于女性与财富的演讲，很多女性第一次接触投资的机会都是通过 401(k) 和雇主。

turns.en: And now you have Trump accounts.
turns.zh: 而现在，你有了 Trump 账户。

turns.en: For babies, like everybody's getting involved and there'll be just better education and awareness of investing over time. As far as the product selection process, we were selected as a participating product, VTI. So for the babies as they grow up and they decide, hey, maybe 500 securities and SPYM isn't doing it for me, they can add another 3,000 with VTI.
turns.zh: 给婴儿用的。所以每个人都在参与进来，随着时间推移，会有更好的投资者教育和认知。至于产品选择流程，我们（Vanguard）被选为参与产品之一，也就是 VTI。所以这些婴儿长大后，如果他们说「嘿，500 只证券、SPYM 可能不够用了」，他们可以通过 VTI 再增加 3000 只股票的敞口。

turns.en: We were really happy.
turns.zh: 我们真的非常高兴。

turns.en: By the way, how big.
turns.zh: 顺便问一下，那次——

turns.en: Was the party when you got that? when they said you're going to be the default ticker. Did you guys just like take the night off? What was that like?
turns.zh: 庆祝会有多热闹？当他们告诉你们「你们将成为默认代码」时，你们是当晚就放假了吗？那是什么感觉？

turns.en: Took the week off. It was incredible. We were so pleased.
turns.zh: 放了一整周的假。太不可思议了。我们太高兴了。

turns.en: Not only because it's a great opportunity for the fund, obviously, but because we really believe in Spiam. We really believe in the two basis points. We really believe in investing in birth to retirement and after retirement.
turns.zh: 不仅仅是因为这对基金本身是个绝佳的机会，当然这也是原因之一，但更是因为我们真心相信 SPYM。我们真心相信 2 个基点的费率。我们真心相信「从出生到退休、乃至退休之后」的投资理念。

turns.en: So that was incredible.
turns.zh: 所以那感觉真是太棒了。

turns.en: Elise, do you have any questions for Anna about how they got that deal?
turns.zh: Elise，你有什么想问 Anna 的，关于她们是怎么拿下这个默认位置的？

turns.en: I think I know. It's called two basis points versus three.
turns.zh: 我大概知道。就是 2 个基点对 3 个基点。

turns.en: So I wrote a note, which you didn't like, that I thought IVV will cut to two because you guys aren't going to just, you know, let... You're not going to take that lying down?
turns.zh: 我曾经写过一份报告，你可能不太喜欢——我判断 IVV 会降到 2 个基点，因为你们不会就这么——你们不会甘愿挨打吧？

turns.en: I didn't not like it. I didn't agree with it.
turns.zh: 我不是不喜欢，我是不认同。

turns.en: Fair enough. Okay, let's shift gears here to a bombshell filing this week. On Monday, BlackRock filed for ETFs. These are exchange-traded interval funds. I posted just the filing on LinkedIn. It wasn't really a very long post. I had not got that much engagement on a post probably in 10 years over there.
turns.zh: 说得通。好，让我们换个话题，聊聊本周的一枚重磅申报。周一，BlackRock 提交了 ETIF 的申报——这是「交易所交易的间隔基金」（exchange-traded interval funds）。我把这份申报文件发到了 LinkedIn 上，帖子本身并不长。可能十年来，我在 LinkedIn 上从没有哪条帖子收到过那么多的互动。

turns.en: What's an ETF? Okay.
turns.zh: 什么是 ETIF？好的。

turns.en: So an ETF would- You're.
turns.zh: 所以 ETIF 基本上会——你——

turns.en: Going to do it?
turns.zh: 要自己讲吗？

turns.en: Would basically take it- I kind of want to see what he says.
turns.zh: 基本上会——我还挺想听听他怎么说的。

turns.en: ETF.
turns.zh: ETIF——

turns.en: It's basically trying to combine an interval fund, which would have private company and private credit exposure into an ETF structure. You wouldn't be able to do creation to redemption all the time. In the end, it would be something like a closed end fund ETF hybrid. It would still trade on an exchange, but there would definitely be deviations because you wouldn't have the liquidity you would have.
turns.zh: 它基本上是想把间隔基金（interval fund）——里面会包含私营公司和私募信贷敞口——塞进 ETF 的结构里。你不会一直都能进行申购和赎回。最终它有点像是封闭式基金和 ETF 的混合体：仍然会在交易所挂牌交易，但一定会出现偏离，因为你无法拥有像 ETF 那样的流动性。

turns.en: Interesting week, Elyse, to do this since we're talking to you on the day that Anthropic happens to IPO.
turns.zh: 很有意思的一周，Elise——之所以选在这周做这件事，是因为我们跟你对话的当天，正好是 Anthropic 上市的日子。

turns.en: Yeah, and so I don't blame everybody for wanting these cool, hot shot private companies. I know you're probably going to say I can't talk because it's in registration, but what can you say, if anything?
turns.zh: 是的，所以我并不怪大家都想拿到这些酷炫、热门的私营公司。我知道你可能会说「我不能讲，因为还在注册期」，但你能说点什么吗？哪怕一点点？

turns.en: First of all, I'm glad I helped you with your LinkedIn engagement, so you're welcome. I think you explained it well. This is taking the investment flexibility of an interval fund, and it's combining it with the convenience and the exchange-traded experience of an ETF. We all know that the hardest part of accessing privates is that you need You know, the minimums are high. You have to deal with the subscription paperwork. That takes all of this away. And so the biggest distinction here is that in a traditional interval fund, you're basically paying for liquidity with time, right? So you have to wait for the window to open to get the redemptions, and then it might be prorated. With an ETIF, you're basically paying for liquidity with price, right? So there is the potential that this is going to trade at a discount to NAV, especially when markets are stressed. And so I think the big thing to understand here is like, we're not trying to change the liquidity characteristics of privates. They are what they are, but we're trying to innovate around how to have people have access and just have greater choices to how they want to implement this in their portfolio.
turns.zh: 首先，我很高兴帮你的 LinkedIn 互动量做了贡献，不用谢。我觉得你解释得很好。这就是把间隔基金的投资灵活性，与 ETF 的便利性和交易所交易体验结合起来。我们都知道，接触私募资产最难的地方在于最低投资门槛很高，还要处理认购文件——ETIF 把这些统统消除了。所以这里最大的区别是：在传统间隔基金中，你其实是用时间来换取流动性——你必须等赎回窗口打开，然后可能还会被按比例缩减；而在 ETIF 中，你是用价格来换取流动性——所以它有可能相对 NAV 折价交易，尤其是在市场承压的时候。我认为最需要理解的一点是：我们并不是要改变私募资产本身的流动性属性，它是什么样就是什么样；我们是要在「如何让人们有机会接触、并拥有更多选择如何将其纳入自己组合」这个层面去创新。

turns.en: Anna, how do you feel that a lease and company came up with that idea and not State Street?
turns.zh: Anna，你有什么感觉——Elise 的公司想出了这个主意，而不是 State Street？

turns.en: You're being really hard on it.
turns.zh: 你这也太狠了。

turns.en: I'll take it.
turns.zh: 我认了。

turns.en: So, First of all, I think it's brilliant. Second of all, I hate it that they came up with.
turns.zh: 首先，我觉得这个主意非常聪明。其次，我很讨厌居然被她们——

turns.en: The idea first.
turns.zh: 抢先想到了。

turns.en: Thank you for the honesty.
turns.zh: 谢谢你的坦诚。

turns.en: Honestly, I truly, truly hate it. But I also love it because this is the beauty of this industry. somebody comes up with a great idea, we can all build on that great idea and we can all really create new things that meet our client's objective. So yes, I hated it that I didn't come up with the idea first, but now that there is a great idea in market, we can all build on that.
turns.zh: 说真的，我真的、真的很不爽。但同时我也很喜欢它，因为这正是这个行业的魅力所在：有人想出一个好主意，我们所有人都可以在这个好主意之上继续构建，一起创造新的东西，去满足我们客户的目标。所以，是的，我很不爽自己没能第一个想到；但现在市面上有了这个好主意，我们大家都能在上面继续做文章。

turns.en: And Janelle, what have you learned about ETFs with the enthusiasm for private companies and ETFs? What have you learned about them?
turns.zh: Janelle，围绕私募公司进入 ETF 这股热潮，你对 ETF 又有了哪些新的认识？

turns.en: I'm going nunchucks again. So yeah, I think the structures are interesting. We're in the spirit of democratizing asset classes, so I like that there's an opportunity for investors to get access to an asset class where maybe they haven't been able to in the past. But I don't know that I love the exposure that you're able to get to privates.
turns.zh: 我又要拿出双节棍了。是的，我觉得这些结构本身很有意思。本着「让各类资产大众化」的精神，我很喜欢看到投资者有机会去接触一个过去可能碰不到的资产类别。但我并不确定，我很喜欢这些载体所能提供的私募敞口——

turns.en: In some of these vehicles.
turns.zh: 在其中的一些载体里。

turns.en: Can you be more specific?
turns.zh: 你能说得具体一点吗？

turns.en: You know, if there's like a, I don't know with the new products, we'll see how these go. But like today, if there's a 15% cap on what actual private investments are in the ETF structure, it's kind of just a watered down version of what I think investors really want out of their private investment sleeve. So I tend to think that the illiquidity premium doesn't belong in a liquid vehicle so you can get more juice out of the squeeze. But if that's the only way that you can access private markets, I still think it's an interesting option.
turns.zh: 你知道，如果——我不太清楚新产品会怎么样，我们会拭目以待。但就今天而言，如果 ETF 结构中对实际私募投资的比例上限只有 15%，那这就有点像稀释版本，跟投资者真正想从私募配置中拿到的东西不太一样。所以我倾向于认为，非流动性溢价并不属于一个流动性载体——你想通过承担非流动性来榨出更多汁水。但如果这是你唯一能接触私募市场的途径，我仍然觉得这是一个有意思的选择。

turns.en: Okay, let's turn to AI. Janelle, we'll start with you because AI, all three of you are probably doing many interesting things with it. The advisor world is probably going to change very rapidly. So just give us your top thing that you're thinking about in regards to AI and how it's going to impact our industry.
turns.zh: 好，让我们转向 AI。Janelle，从你开始——因为 AI，你们三位可能都在做很多有意思的事情。投顾行业很可能会非常快速地发生变化。所以就聊聊你在 AI 方面最关心的一个问题：它将如何影响我们这个行业？

turns.en: I think AI today is impacting just every part of a product. So it's front office through distribution. So we've come up with a number of tools on our active management products that, you know, we used to have folks spending hours doing research or fighting with Microsoft Excel, and now they're able to use, develop, have their own agents and tools. to have a more efficient and timely process. So hopefully it's more alpha in the portfolios over time as well. On the distribution side, I mean, it's really tough for advisors to understand the impact as to how they're thinking about asset allocation and portfolio construction. And I think we're seeing their roles evolve beyond what used to be the sexy parts of the job to more of, I have a friend who's here who runs her own RIA and she said, hey, half of my job is being a therapist. I do a lot more work around behavioral finance and estate planning, healthcare planning, helping people just be prepared and spending a lot less time on asset allocation, portfolio construction. So that's where I see AI really coming into play and being helpful, but it won't really replace the value of humanity or human touch.
turns.zh: 我认为 AI 今天已经在影响一只产品的每一个环节——从前台到分销。所以我们在主动管理产品线上开发了很多工具，过去员工要花好几个小时做研究，或者跟 Microsoft Excel 搏斗，现在他们可以开发、拥有自己的 agent 和工具，让整个流程更高效、更及时。所以也希望随着时间推移，组合里能出现更多的 alpha。在分销端，投顾要理解 AI 对他们思考资产配置和组合构建的冲击，其实真的很难。我觉得他们的角色正在演变，从过去那些「光鲜」的部分，转向更多——我有一位朋友在这儿，她自己开了一家 RIA，她说：「嘿，我一半的工作是当心理治疗师。」我做了大量围绕行为金融、遗产规划、医疗规划的工作，帮助人们做好准备，而在资产配置和组合构建上花的时间则少得多。所以这正是我看到 AI 真正能派上用场、提供帮助的地方，但它并不会真正取代人性的价值，或者人与人接触的价值。

turns.en: Elise, how are you using AI So I think there's two compelling use cases for AI.
turns.zh: Elise，你们是怎么用 AI 的？我觉得 AI 有两个很有说服力的用例。

turns.en: The first is just in product innovation, right?
turns.zh: 第一个就是在产品创新方面，对吧？

turns.en: AI can really help us design, test, and think about the underlying construction of our new innovation. That's not wild or hot sauce, but like our new innovation. And I think that frees up time for the teams to actually spend with our clients and understand what they're asking for, what they need and what solutions we're actually trying to solve. And then the second is what Janelle just articulated, right? It's more about the investor experience. The more and more we can make discoverable through AI, the more education we can give on some of these sophisticated strategies will help them implement this into their portfolios.
turns.zh: AI 真的可以帮助我们设计、测试并思考新产品的底层构建方式——注意，我说的不是那种疯狂或「辣椒酱」型的产品，而是我们真正意义上的创新。我觉得这也把团队的时间释放出来，让他们可以真正花在客户身上，去理解客户在问什么、需要什么，我们究竟要解决什么问题。第二个用例就是 Janelle 刚才讲到的，就是投资者体验。我们越能通过 AI 让内容可被发现，就越能给投资者提供更多关于复杂策略的教育，帮助他们以正确的方式把这些策略纳入自己的组合。

turns.en: In the right way.
turns.zh: 用正确的方式。

turns.en: Anna, any particular uses that you're fond of?
turns.zh: Anna，你有什么特别喜欢的 AI 应用吗？

turns.en: What I really like about AI is that it's helping us really well unpack flows. Because when it comes to ETFs, I mean, you guys know that, it's really, really hard to trace flows back to the end investor and to understand what channel those flows are coming from. So AI is really helping us get smarter, get to the information faster, and be much more surgical when it comes to building research, building education, or knowing exactly who is going to consume it.
turns.zh: 我特别喜欢 AI 的一点是，它帮助我们非常精细地拆解资金流。因为说到 ETF，你们也知道，要把资金流追溯到最终投资者、要搞清楚这些资金流来自哪个渠道，是非常非常困难的。所以 AI 真的在帮助我们变得更聪明、更快拿到信息，并且在构建研究、构建教育内容，或者在准确判断「谁会消费这些内容」时，做到更加精准。

turns.en: Okay, let's turn to the youth. I remember back in the day, somebody was floating around saying, how can Vanguard reach millennials? Now it's like 10 years later. It's how can ETF issuers reach Gen Z and even lower? My 15-year-old is in a stock market club in school, and they worship this guy named TJR, Finfluencer. And in Asia, that's a big deal there. You guys have Finfluencer salespeople. And there's a guy who his whole job is to get ETF issuers in front of Finfluencers in the U.S., So clearly this is a growing market. Some people are going to blow it off as silly, but a lot of people follow these people. And I want to know what you're doing to reach the young people so they're not like, oh, that's from boomer parent stuff. It's cool.
turns.zh: 好，让我们把话题转向年轻人。我记得当年，还有人到处在讨论「Vanguard 该怎么触达千禧一代」。现在过了差不多 10 年，问题变成了「ETF 发行商该怎么触达 Gen Z，甚至更小的孩子」。我 15 岁的孩子在学校的股票社团里，他们崇拜一个叫 TJR 的 finfluencer（金融网红）。在亚洲，这可是件大事。你们那边也有 finfluencer 型的销售员。有个人，他的整份工作就是让 ETF 发行商出现在美国 finfluencer 面前。所以很显然，这是一个正在增长的市场。有些人会觉得这事儿很傻，但有很多人跟随这些人。我想知道，你们在做什么去触达年轻人，让他们不会觉得「哦，那是我 boomer 父母那辈的东西」，而是觉得「这很酷」？

turns.en: Janelle. I love that you really date yourself by saying the youth.
turns.zh: Janelle——我很欣赏你，居然用「年轻人」这种说法把自己年龄暴露了。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.en: I sound like I'm from 1950.
turns.zh: 我听起来像是 1950 年来的。

turns.en: These young whippersnappers. The youngsters.
turns.zh: 这些年轻的小屁孩。这些「小伙子」。

turns.en: The whippersnappers. Okay.
turns.zh: 小屁孩。好的。

turns.en: You know, I view them as any other client segment in that we have to reach them.
turns.zh: 你知道，我把他们看作和其他任何客户群体一样，我们必须去触达他们——

turns.en: Where they are.
turns.zh: 在他们所在的地方。

turns.en: And if they're engaging and learning and education about the industry through social media, we have to have a presence there and we have to have the right partnerships with folks who they follow. So we have had work done with influencers. I think it's okay for me to name one.
turns.zh: 如果他们是通过社交媒体来参与、学习和了解这个行业，那我们就必须在那里有存在感，也必须和他们关注的这些人建立合适的合作关系。所以我们已经和一些网红有过合作。我觉得提一个人的名字应该没关系——

turns.en: It's Mrs.
turns.zh: 是 Mrs.

turns.en: Dow Jones. We've done some things with her.
turns.zh: Dow Jones。我们和她做过一些合作。

turns.en: And I think it's been more of helping people understand beyond like the gamification of investing, what's actually going on, and then beyond just the impact to them as individuals in their portfolios, what they can do beyond that, like participate in our investor choice program, knowing that they can choose the way that they're going to vote their own proxy and helping them see that there's a lot more that they can do to change the world than just receive the returns from their investment portfolio.
turns.zh: 我觉得这更多是帮助大家理解，除了投资的游戏化之外，实际上到底在发生什么；也让他们看到，除了作为个人、他们的组合会受到的影响之外，他们还能做什么——比如参与我们的 investor choice 项目，知道自己可以选择如何去投出自己的代理投票权，帮助他们看到，除了从投资组合里获得回报之外，他们还可以做很多事情去改变这个世界。

turns.en: For us, it's a little bit of a test and learn because this is new territory. And we haven't been in this territory before. So we need to learn what new language we have to use, new words, new concepts, new way of approaching this young generation. And Finfluencers are a way to do that. But again, we are in the test and learn phase because it's harder to understand the reach of these influencers. Just to give you an example, we worked with a Finfluencer that I'm not going to name. And here comes the first post about SPY. and within minutes, five million views. And I was like, OMG, great investment. And then the feed goes by, three or four minutes down, the same influencer, and now I will explain to you why Voo is my best choice.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，这有点像是「测试与学习」，因为这是一片新领域。我们以前从没涉足过。所以我们需要去学习要用什么样的新语言、新词汇、新概念，以及接触这一代年轻人的新方式。Finfluencer 是其中一种做法。但同样，我们仍然处在测试和学习阶段，因为很难搞清楚这些网红的实际触达面。举个例子，我们和一位 finfluencer 合作过——我不打算说出名字。第一条关于 SPY 的帖子发出来后，几分钟之内，500 万次浏览。我当时想，天啊，太划算了。然后信息流往下刷，三四分钟之后，同一个网红又出现了：「现在让我来告诉你，为什么 VOO 是我的最佳选择。」

turns.en: What?
turns.zh: 什么？

turns.en: This is so wrong.
turns.zh: 这也太离谱了。

turns.en: So again, we are testing and learning who to work with, the information that we give, and obviously the results that we are receiving through that.
turns.zh: 所以，我们仍然在测试和学习：该和谁合作、我们给出的信息、以及我们从中收到的结果。

turns.en: But this is why this industry is so fun, right? Like, I want to come back as its influencer.
turns.zh: 但这也正是为什么这个行业这么有意思，对吧？我下辈子想回来当一个网红。

turns.en: I think that, you know, it's not just young investors, right, that are learning from these different channels. Like you have all investors that are changing the way they're educating themselves every day. And so we have also been working with financial content creators just through like, how do you make it real life? How do you bring them into some of these industry forums or experiences where they have the opportunity to meet with investment experts, right?
turns.zh: 我觉得，你知道，不仅仅是年轻投资者在通过这些不同的渠道学习。所有投资者每天都在改变自己获取教育的方式。所以我们也在和一些财经内容创作者合作，比如：怎么把这些内容变得贴近现实生活？怎么把他们带到一些行业论坛或体验活动中，让他们有机会与投资专家见面？

turns.en: Influencers aren't licensed, right?
turns.zh: 网红并没有牌照，对吧？

turns.en: And so it's our job to actually help educate them and make sure that they have trusted investment expertise that they're putting out there to all the people that follow them.
turns.zh: 所以我们的工作是真正帮助他们接受教育，确保他们对外发布给所有关注他们的人的内容，具备可信的投资专业性。

turns.en: And I think that's pretty cool. It's a whole new avenue of people.
turns.zh: 我觉得这一点还挺酷的。这是一整条全新的人群通道。

turns.en: I'm curious if you did come back as a finfluencer. Do you want to pitch that to me?
turns.zh: 我很好奇，如果你真的回来当一个 finfluencer——你想跟我推销一下这个人设吗？

turns.en: I have to think about my name. Maybe it's like Nunchucks. I don't know, but we'll figure it out.
turns.zh: 我得想想我的名字。也许就叫「双节棍」之类的。我不知道，我们会想出来的。

turns.en: But I don't think it's just a finfluencer. What we are really.
turns.zh: 但我觉得并不仅仅是 finfluencer。我们现在真正——

turns.en: spending time on right now is also how do you get into the LLMs? Because, you know, Eric, your son is 15. I have two, 14 and 13. One thing I know for sure is that they are never going to walk into a bank. They are never going to sit down with a financial advisor for two hours talking about their investment objective and risk.
turns.zh: 花时间的地方，还有怎么才能进入 LLM。因为你知道，Eric，你儿子 15 岁；我有两个孩子，14 岁和 13 岁。我唯一确定的一件事是：他们永远不会走进一家银行，也永远不会和一位理财顾问坐下来聊上两个小时，讨论自己的投资目标和风险——

turns.en: Propensity. They are going to use an LLM.
turns.zh: 偏好。他们会用 LLM。

turns.en: And how do you get your education inside of charge EPTs, Gemini's, pick your SI or AI and you'll find the answer. But to me, that's like, it's not just influencers. It's not just social media. This next generation, you are going to have to reach them everywhere. They consume information.
turns.zh: 那么，你怎么把你的教育内容塞进 ChatGPT、Gemini——随便你选哪个 AI，都能找到答案。但对我来说，这已经不只是网红、不只是社交媒体了。对下一代，你必须在他们所有获取信息的地方都能触达他们。

turns.en: I mean, you know, how are you, how are you talking about that at Vanguard? Because I mean, you, there's a lot of financial advisors out there that you want to try and reach though. And like potential is that they're going to be disintermediated here. How are you guys talking about that?
turns.zh: 我是说，你们知道，在 Vanguard 内部你们是怎么讨论这件事的吗？因为外面还有很多理财顾问是你们想触达的。但有一种可能性是，他们会被「去中介化」。你们是怎么讨论这个问题的？

turns.en: I was over here thinking about what I was going to change my Instagram name to, and I'm thinking big beta.
turns.zh: 我刚才在这边一直在想，我要把我的 Instagram 名字改成什么，我在想要不就叫「Big Beta」。

turns.en: So I'll let you guys move to the next question.
turns.zh: 所以我就让你们进入下一个问题吧。

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Well, you're all stewards in the ETF industry. And even just talking about influencers there for a second. What could go wrong? I mean, this is a week where all kinds of tech snafus have happened. Anthropic IPOs, risk is a thing that they're talking about. What could go wrong as we kind of look around the corner a little bit, Elyse?
turns.zh: 嗯，你们都是 ETF 行业的守护者。哪怕只是刚才聊到网红那一小段——会出什么问题？我的意思是，这一周各种技术故障层出不穷，Anthropic 上市，风险是大家一直在讨论的话题。往前稍微看一步，Elise，会出什么问题？

turns.en: Yeah, I think, look, it comes back to making sure you're engaging with that credibility, the education, making sure there's responsible innovation happening and people understand what they're buying. When you ask what could go wrong, it's that someone buys a 2X or 3X product and just doesn't understand what the downside of that is. And there's absolutely people that want to invest in those products and it's for them and that's why those products are there. I worry about the investors that might not be as educated and may watch an Instagram post or something from someone a little wacky that does not have the content 100% correct. And then they go and invest it and they have a really bad experience.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得，你看，最终还是要确保你在与投资者互动时具备可信度、具备教育意义，确保创新是负责任的、人们知道自己在买什么。当你问「会出什么问题」时，那就是有人买了一只 2 倍或 3 倍杠杆的产品，却根本不明白它的下行风险是什么。当然有人就是想投资这类产品，这些产品就是为他们准备的，这也是这些产品存在的原因。我担心的是那些受教育程度可能没那么高的投资者，他们可能刷到一条 Instagram 帖子，或者来自某个内容并不 100% 正确的、有点古怪的人的东西，然后就去投资，结果经历非常糟糕。

turns.en: That's, in my mind, what could go wrong.
turns.zh: 在我看来，这就是可能出问题的地方。

turns.en: Anna?
turns.zh: Anna？

turns.en: I agree with that because I always say that when people talk about good investment decisions or bad investment decisions... That's not the right way to characterize decisions. Decisions are either informed or uninformed. There is a reason why we are all licensed. There is a reason why only licensed individuals can talk about securities and make financial recommendations. There is now a number of people exchanging information that is not always accurate. And to me, that leads to uninformed investment decisions. That's the biggest risk. And that is gonna spoil it for everybody.
turns.zh: 我同意这一点，因为我一直说，当人们谈论好的投资决策或坏的投资决策时……这并不是描述决策的正确方式。决策要么是「知情」的，要么是「不知情」的。我们所有人之所以持牌，是有原因的；只有持牌人士才能谈论证券、给出财务建议，这也是有原因的。现在有相当多的人在传递并不总是准确的信息。对我来说，这会导致「不知情」的投资决策。这就是最大的风险。而且这会把整锅汤都毁了，对谁都没好处。

turns.en: So much of like what you get out of AI also is based off of what you put into it. And if you're not asking the right questions or prompts, you might miss information that's really important. So say if somebody were here talking about a great product that they have and the expense ratio is two basis points, but they're not talking about spreads or volatility of premiums and discounts, they might end up getting into a product at a price that they're not comfortable with or maybe not get the return that they were expecting. So garbage in, garbage out.
turns.zh: 你从 AI 那里得到的很多东西，也取决于你输入了什么。如果你没有问对问题、没有用对提示词，你可能会错过一些非常重要的信息。比方说，如果有人在这里介绍一款很棒的产品，费率是 2 个基点，但他们不谈价差、不谈溢价折价的波动性，那投资者最终可能会以一个自己并不舒服的价格买入，或者可能拿不到自己预期的回报。所以就是「垃圾进，垃圾出」。

turns.en: Two basis points is still good.
turns.zh: 但 2 个基点毕竟还是很好的。

turns.en: Just real quick, our solution at BI is the traffic light system, which is roughly like movie ratings. And the leverage get like a red light. I just think the brokerages should have that. And it just tells you why it's dangerous. It'll be very quick. I don't know why that hasn't been adopted, but if anybody out there wants to talk to me afterwards, this should be the solution. Anyway, pontification over.
turns.zh: 简单说一下，我们在 Bloomberg Intelligence 的解决方案是「红绿灯系统」，大致类似于电影分级。杠杆型产品会亮红灯。我只是觉得券商应该采用这个。它会告诉你为什么某只产品是危险的，非常简洁。我不知道为什么这个还没有被采用，但如果外面有人想事后找我聊聊，我认为这就是答案。好了，说教结束。

turns.en: Great upsell right there.
turns.zh: 很好的推销。

turns.en: Okay, tokenization is... I just did this whole project on crypto. I was moved a little closer to being a believer, but I still am.
turns.zh: 好，代币化——我刚做完一整个关于加密的项目，我离「信徒」近了一点，但我仍然——

turns.en: I don't understand. You have your phone.
turns.zh: 我不明白。你有你的手机——

turns.en: You can type in any ticker on a brokerage platform and get almost everything for no fee instantly. No one cares if it takes a day to go through the system. So what is tokenization really solving here and how Are we going to be in 10 years the tokenization event here? Will ETFs be double where they are? Where do you see, how much is tokenization going to dent this growth? Let's start with you on the end, Elise.
turns.zh: 你可以在券商平台上输入任何代码，几乎零费用、瞬间就能买到几乎所有东西。没人在乎走完整个系统要花一天。所以代币化到底在解决什么问题？10 年之后，我们会在哪里？「代币化事件」会是什么样？ETF 规模会翻倍吗？你怎么看，代币化会对这一轮增长造成多大冲击？从坐在最边上的 Elise 开始。

turns.en: So Eric, I felt the same way. And then I went to get my haircut one day. And my hairdresser was telling me how, she was asking about Bitcoin. And I was like, oh, do you own iBit? And she was like, no, I own Bitcoin.
turns.zh: Eric，我原来也和你感觉一样。然后有一天我去剪头发，我的发型师在问我关于 Bitcoin 的事情。我就问：「哦，你持有 IBIT 吗？」她说：「不，我持有 Bitcoin。」

turns.en: And I was like, oh. And she's like, I've owned it since 2015. And then she- Oh.
turns.zh: 我就「哦」了一声。然后她说：「我从 2015 年就开始持有了。」然后她——哦。

turns.en: My God, I would have loved to have been here for this.
turns.zh: 天啊，我真希望当时能在场听这段。

turns.en: Well- I was quiet and then she explained how she doesn't like big banks and she doesn't like big custodians and she named a lot of them and she went through this whole thing and she has everything in her wallet and that's where she wants to invest and that's where she's comfortable investing and it really did open my eyes that there is this whole wide world of investors that just don't want to do it the way we do it traditionally. And there's millions upon millions of wallets. And so that is an entire ecosystem of investors that we can touch if we tokenize our ETFs. And so I don't think it kills ETFs. I don't think it ends us. I think it's just another access point and it's providing choice.
turns.zh: 嗯——我当时没说话，然后她开始解释她如何不喜欢大银行、不喜欢大托管机构，还点了很多家的名字，把整套逻辑讲了一遍。她所有的资产都在自己的钱包里，那就是她想投资的地方，也是她觉得舒服的投资方式。这真的让我大开眼界：原来外面有整整一个广阔的投资者世界，他们根本不想按我们传统的方式来。而且这样的钱包有千千万万。所以如果我们把 ETF 代币化，就能触达一整片投资者生态。所以我不认为这会杀死 ETF，我不认为这会终结我们。我觉得这只是又一个入口，是在提供选择。

turns.en: Janelle, how about for Vanguard?
turns.zh: Janelle，那 Vanguard 呢？

turns.en: I mean, I feel like we talk so much about customization.
turns.zh: 我是说，我觉得我们花了太多时间在讲定制化。

turns.en: And I remember talking about this years ago about direct indexing and SMAs being.
turns.zh: 我记得多年前就在讨论 direct indexing 和 SMA 会成为——

turns.en: The ETF killer.
turns.zh: ETF 杀手。

turns.en: Now it's like, is tokenization going to be the ETF killer? There's something that's always trying to kill these ETFs. But I do think it's an interesting opportunity for improving.
turns.zh: 现在又变成：代币化会不会是 ETF 杀手？总有些东西在试图杀死 ETF。但我确实认为，这是一个改进——

turns.en: That type of process.
turns.zh: 那种流程的有趣机会。

turns.en: So maybe some other types of vehicles or other structures where things are going to be bigger, better, faster in the future. We just don't know what that holds, but we certainly can't ignore it.
turns.zh: 所以未来也许会出现一些其他类型的载体或者其他结构，让某些环节变得更大、更好、更快。我们还不知道那会是什么样子，但我们绝对不能忽视它。

turns.en: Anna, anything more about tokenization that excites you?
turns.zh: Anna，代币化里还有什么让你兴奋的点吗？

turns.en: Well, you know, it's all about the use case. We tokenized our first money market fund in April because there was a clear use case. Collateral, they wanted it on T plus zero seconds. They didn't want it on T plus one. So the use case for that was very compelling. Use case for ETFs may become compelling when all of these portfolios will converge because I do agree that there is a user population that doesn't like traditional big banks and the big banking. But I don't think it's going to kill ETFs. The pie is going to grow. The market is going to grow. People are going to come to ETFs through different channels. I don't think this is going to be the ETF killer at all.
turns.zh: 你知道，这一切都要看用例。今年 4 月我们把自己第一只货币市场基金代币化了，因为有一个非常清晰的用例：作为抵押品，他们希望是 T+0 秒到账，而不是 T+1。所以这个用例非常有说服力。ETF 的用例可能要在所有组合汇聚到一起时才会变得有说服力——我确实同意，有一部分用户群体不喜欢传统大银行、不喜欢大银行体系。但我并不认为这会杀死 ETF。蛋糕会继续变大，市场会继续增长，人们会通过不同的渠道来到 ETF。我完全不觉得这会是 ETF 杀手。

turns.en: All right, we've entered the final stages of the episode. This is the part that you all came for. Janelle, what do you like most about the competitors to your left?
turns.zh: 好，我们已经进入本期节目的最后阶段。这就是你们都在等的部分。Janelle，坐在你左边的这些竞争对手，你最欣赏她们哪一点？

turns.en: To be clear, the two basis point was not at all about SPYM.
turns.zh: 先说清楚，我们降到 2 个基点，跟 SPYM 一点关系都没有。

turns.en: It was another presenter earlier in the day, and I think you guys all know who that was. You know, these are two very reputable, respected organizations. And if they weren't, they wouldn't be the size that they are. And we wouldn't be on the stage together. I mean, we're all women in the industry. And I look up to both of these women. I know their jobs are hard and I respect what they do. Specifically, I would like to say, you know, I love what State Street is doing with their product lineup. I think the two of us were thought of as kind of like stodgy, kind of stalled out from a product launch perspective. And I think we're doing a lot more to cater to investors and give them more low cost options.
turns.zh: 是因为当天早些时候的另一位演讲嘉宾，我想你们都知道是谁。你知道，这是两家非常有声望、受人尊敬的机构。如果不是这样，她们也不会做到今天这样的规模，我们也不会有机会一起坐在这个舞台上。我是说，我们都是这个行业里的女性，两位我都很敬佩。我知道她们的工作很难，我也尊重她们所做的事情。具体来说，我想说，我很喜欢 State Street 在她们的产品线上的动作。我觉得我们两家过去都被认为有点老派、有点在产品发行上停滞不前；而我觉得我们正在做更多事情去迎合投资者、给他们提供更多低成本的选择。

turns.en: So I really appreciate that you all are.
turns.zh: 所以我真的很感激你们——

turns.en: Doing that work.
turns.zh: 在做这些工作。

turns.en: BlackRock, you guys have always been good at that.
turns.zh: BlackRock，你们在这方面一直都做得很好。

turns.en: And something else you're really good at that I respect is building great CEOs.
turns.zh: 还有一件你们真的很擅长、我也很敬佩的事，就是培养出了很多优秀的 CEO。

turns.en: So thanks for that.
turns.zh: 所以谢谢你们的这一点。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: That's cathartic, I'm sure. Anna, how about for you?
turns.zh: 这一定很解压，我相信。Anna，那你呢？

turns.en: Well, if the question is, what would you steal from your competitors?
turns.zh: 如果问题是「你会想从竞争对手那里偷点什么」的话——

turns.en: I have a long list.
turns.zh: 我的清单很长。

turns.en: So first of all, a couple of trillion dollars.
turns.zh: 所以第一，从她们每一家那里各偷几万亿美元。

turns.en: From each one of them.
turns.zh: 从每一家都偷几万亿。

turns.en: Because I do think size and scale matter. With size and scale, you can produce high-quality products at really low fees. So I do think that that matters. But I would take, you know, from Vanguard, I would take Altruist, and I would take the direct-to-consumer platform, which I think is incredibly important. From BlackRock, I would take Aladdin, and I would take their private markets and their new exemptive order application.
turns.zh: 因为我确实认为规模和体量是重要的。有了规模和体量，你才能以非常低的费率做出高质量的产品。所以我认为这一点很重要。但我会「偷」的话——从 Vanguard，我会拿走 Altruist，会拿走那个直销（direct-to-consumer）平台，我觉得这个极其重要。从 BlackRock，我会拿走 Aladdin，会拿走她们的私募市场业务，还有她们新提交的豁免申请（exemptive order application）。

turns.en: That's like the whole thing.
turns.zh: 这基本上就是整个人家了。

turns.en: Are you looking for a job? No, thank you. I love mine.
turns.zh: 你是在找工作吗？不用了，谢谢。我很爱我现在的工作。

turns.en: If my boss is listening, I love my job. Because I really believe in vertical integration, and all these pieces would make for the perfect vertically integrated organization.
turns.zh: 如果我老板在听——我很爱我的工作。因为我真的相信垂直一体化，所有这些拼在一起，会构成一家完美的垂直一体化机构。

turns.en: Elise, are you coming for Janelle's nunchucks?
turns.zh: Elise，你要来抢 Janelle 的双节棍吗？

turns.en: No, no, no.
turns.zh: 不，不，不。

turns.en: I would say, first of all, utter respect. I think this is what makes the industry so great. We get called the big three a lot. I actually think that is the title of this. It makes us seem a little similar, but we actually have such different and distinct histories and business models. The really easy one for Vanguard is that you have this powerful relationship with the end investor through your captive distribution.
turns.zh: 我想说，首先是彻底的尊重。我觉得这正是这个行业如此伟大的地方。我们经常被称为「三巨头」，其实我觉得这就是这期节目的标题。这个称呼让我们看起来有点相似，但我们其实有着非常不同、非常独特的历史和商业模式。对 Vanguard 来说，最容易「羡慕」的一点是：通过你们自有的分销渠道，你们和终端投资者之间建立了非常强大的关系。

turns.en: I will come for your direct channel any day of the week. I love it. We wouldn't be.
turns.zh: 我随时都愿意来抢你们的直销渠道，任何时候。我太喜欢它了。如果不是 State Street 帮助这个行业不断创新——

turns.en: Sitting here without State Street helping innovate into this industry. And I think you've kept that spirit of innovation and it just makes everyone better.
turns.zh: 我们也不会坐在这里。我觉得你们保留了那种创新精神，这让每个人都变得更好。

turns.en: So I could go on, but I'll stop there.
turns.zh: 所以我还能继续说下去，但我就到这里吧。

turns.en: All right. Now, what do you hate most about? Where's the PR people? They're sweating right now. Don't worry. Unless you feel like answering. Elise, Anna, Janelle, thank you so much for joining us at Trillions and being at ETFs in depth with us. Thanks for listening to Trillions. Until next time, you can find us on the Bloomberg Terminal, Bloomberg.com, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever else you like to listen. We'd love to hear from you. Hit us up. Trillions is produced by Magnus Henriksen and Keshav Pandya. Amy Keene is our executive producer. Cheryl Brumling is the head of Bloomberg Podcasts. Bye.
turns.zh: 好。那么，你们最讨厌对方什么呢？公关团队在哪儿？他们现在肯定在冒汗。别担心，除非你们愿意回答。Elise、Anna、Janelle，非常感谢你们做客 Trillions，也感谢你们参加 ETFs in Depth。感谢大家收听 Trillions。下次再会，你们可以在 Bloomberg Terminal、Bloomberg.com、Apple Podcasts、Spotify，或者任何你喜欢听播客的地方找到我们。我们非常想听到你们的反馈，欢迎来联系我们。Trillions 由 Magnus Henriksen 和 Keshav Pandya 制作，Amy Keene 是我们的执行制作人，Cheryl Brumley 是 Bloomberg Podcasts 的负责人。再见。
